title: Vietnam Aquaculture Farm-to-Export Traceability
thesis: Every harvest lot that a pond delivers to a fictional Mekong Delta seafood processing plant is a custody transfer. Snowflake turns those transfers into traceability-to-registered-pond and flag-precision KPIs, a 7-day custody-break risk score per plant, mass-balance variance anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

persona.name: Tran Minh Chau
persona.role: Head of Traceability and Export Compliance (fictional)

talking_points: Start with the question an export buyer asks: how much of the fish and shrimp we packed can be traced to a registered pond? 40 processing plants across 8 Mekong Delta cities, 5 sourcing models.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to plant-day rows.
The custody-signal chart shows which checks lead to confirmed custody breaks and which mostly produce false-positive flags.
show: Daily harvest-lot custody transfers and custody flags
tabs.call_out: One governed definition of traceable harvest, from pond to export lot

transition.line: Which plants should the traceability team visit first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification ranks plants by the probability of a confirmed custody break in the next 7 days, so farm visits go where they matter.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags mass-balance variance outliers per plant, and the forecast projects network-wide harvest-lot transfers for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: Is the pond registry keeping up?

talking_points: Mass-balance reconciliation rate, pond link coverage across registered farm suppliers, and pond verifications still pending.
The scatter compares each plant's reconciliation rate with its confirmed custody breaks.
tabs.call_out: Close pond-link gaps before the export buyer asks for farm-level evidence

transition.line: What happens when a lot arrives out of tolerance?

talking_points: Harvest-lot custody-transfer events land in RAW.LIVE_TRANSFERS: simulated in Snowflake, or from Amazon Data Firehose through S3 and Snowpipe in the AWS build.
FLAG events (a transfer whose mass-balance variance is out of tolerance) are logged by the alert, which emails the team.
tabs.call_out: From plant receiving dock to custody alert in one platform

persona.name: Tran Minh Chau
persona.role: Head of Traceability and Export Compliance (fictional)

talking_points: The Cortex Agent answers with generated SQL over the semantic view and cites the synthetic chain-of-custody SOPs by ID.
The action memo is drafted only from KPI, plant, custody-signal and risk rows; custody checks are demo signals, not audit or certification verdicts.
show: Agent answer with SQL and SOP citations
tabs.call_out: Answers carry their SQL and SOP IDs, so nobody has to trust a number blindly

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

persona.name: Tran Minh Chau
persona.role: Head of Traceability and Export Compliance (fictional)

talking_points: Both builds share the same core: seeded data, dynamic tables, Snowflake ML, Cortex Search, semantic view, agent, alert and task graph.
The AWS build adds Amazon Data Firehose, S3 and Snowpipe ingestion, a Bedrock memo and a QuickSight dashboard with an Amazon Q topic.
